verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN): the held-out harness found `/app/solution.py`, ran all three SciCode sub-steps, and every one raised an `AssertionError` with reward 0.0 and zero steps passed [1][2]. The task required three coupled functions in `/app/solution.py` for Fourier-domain beam propagation, ABCD-matrix waist tracking through a lens system, and full transmission with focus depth and focal intensity [3], but the agent substituted textbook approximations that diverge from the reference formulation on all three steps. For propagation, the reference uses an angular-spectrum transfer `exp(i·2π·z·sqrt((1/λ)²−fx²−fy²))` with `fftshift`/`ifftshift` and returns the complex field magnitudes without the agent's paraxial `exp(−iπ·λ·z·(fx²+fy²))` shortcut [4][6], which is why hidden test 28.1's integrated-power check fails. For lens transmission, the reference tracks waists via `q=(z−s)+i·z_R/Mp2` piecewise before and after `L1` with `sqrt(Mp2)` scaling, whereas the agent chained generic ABCD matrices from an `R0`-based `q₀` [5][6], producing waist arrays that do not match the HDF5 targets in 28.2. For the top-level simulator, the reference sets focal intensity from the minimized waist `exp(−r²/w_focus²)`, but the agent reused its incorrect propagator at `argmin(Wz)` [5][6], yielding wrong focus depth and intensity in 28.3. After a single write in ~1 minute, the agent ran only a self-chosen smoke test that checked shapes and a hand-waved lens-focus sanity case, then declared all functions correct without comparing outputs to any expected values [7][8], so the failure reflects incorrect implementation rather than a broken verifier.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent submitted numerically incorrect Gaussian-beam physics code that failed all three held-out verifier steps; the FAIL is justified.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN). After the agent finished, the held-out harness found `/app/solution.py` and reported `steps_passed: 0` of 3 with `reward: 0.0`, failing every sub-step on `np.allclose` / `cmp_tuple_or_list` assertion errors against HDF5 reference targets [1]. The task required three coupled functions—Fourier-domain beam propagation, ABCD-matrix waist tracking through a lens system, and a transmission routine that finds focus depth and focus-plane intensity—in a single `/app/solution.py` [2]. The hidden reference implements propagation with an `fftshift`/`ifftshift` Fourier pipeline and a centered frequency grid [3], and computes waists via a complex q-parameter evaluated before and after the `L1` plane [4]. The agent instead wrote its own `/app/solution.py` using unshifted `np.fft.fft2`/`ifft2` for propagation [5] and a different ABCD formulation that loops per-distance matrix products with `q0 = Mp2 / inverse_q0` rather than the reference q-at-lens split [6]. Those implementation choices produce wrong numerical outputs on the verifier's physics checks—e.g., step 28.1 integrates propagated amplitude to compare conserved power `(P1, P2)` against stored targets [8]—so all three steps fail as reported [1]. The agent only self-validated with `py_compile` and a toy run checking array shapes and `np.isfinite` outputs, then declared sanity checks passed without comparing against expected waist values or integrated power [7][9]. The submission therefore does not genuinely solve the benchmark despite being syntactically complete.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct [1][2]. The task required three coupled functions in `/app/solution.py` implementing Fourier-domain beam propagation, ABCD-matrix waist tracking through a lens system, and a combined transmission routine that finds the post-lens focus and intensity field [3]. The agent did write all three functions and declared completion [4][11], but its physics diverges materially from the reference on every sub-step: `propagate_gaussian_beam` uses a paraxial Fresnel filter `exp(-iπλz(fx²+fy²))` with unshifted FFTs instead of the reference angular-spectrum propagator with `fftshift`/`ifftshift` and a `sqrt((1/λ)²-fx²-fy²)` transfer function, causing the hidden 28.1 energy-conservation `np.allclose` on integrated power to fail [5][8]; `gaussian_beam_through_lens` explicitly ignores `L1` and applies only `Mz·Mf1·Ms` ABCD chaining, whereas the reference partitions the axis at `L1` and uses distinct q-parameter formulas before and after the lens, so the hidden 28.2 waist-array comparison also fails [6][7][9]; and `Gussian_Lens_transmission` inherits those upstream errors and squares the z=0 propagated amplitude rather than returning the reference Gaussian intensity profile at the argmin waist, so the hidden 28.3 tuple comparison fails as well [10][2]. The agent relied on shape checks and toy smoke tests that never compared against conserved-energy or reference values [11][12], while the hidden reference solution implements the angular-spectrum propagator, L1-partitioned waist model, and direct Gaussian focus intensity the tests target [13].
